title: URL slugs
description: Title-to-slug generation for server apps: Latin diacritic transliteration and optional Unicode scripts, word-boundary length cap, concurrency-safe unique slugs per tenant scope with numeric suffixes, reserved route words, rename history with 301 redirects that never chain or loop, a PostgreSQL store and a Fetch resolve adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build, String.prototype.normalize, Unicode property escapes and the Fetch Request/Response APIs (http.ts only): Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core usable without http.ts; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlSlugStore (table may be schema-qualified) with a query executor that also offers transaction() (needed for rename); elsewhere implement SlugStore with a unique (scope, slug) key and a unique current slug per (scope, entity).
Build each scope with slugScope(tenantId, collection) from trusted server context, never from the URL or request body.
Pass reserved: [...DEFAULT_RESERVED_SLUGS, ...yourRouteNames] so no slug can shadow a route; set maxLength, separator, unicode and fallback to match your URLs.
Call create when the entity is created, rename when its title or slug changes and remove when it is deleted; store the returned slug on your entity if you need it in listings.

Mount createSlugResolveHandler with routes, prefix and a scopeFor(request, params) that reads the tenant from the session or verified host, or call slugs.resolve from your page handler and issue the redirect yourself.
limitations: Transliterates Latin diacritics (the shared U+00C0-U+017F table plus NFKD decomposition); other scripts are dropped unless unicode is set, so non-Latin titles get the fallback slug in ASCII mode.
Old slugs stay owned by their entity until remove(), so a title can never take a slug another entity once used; there is no expiry or release of single old slugs.
Redirects are cached by browsers for redirectMaxAgeSeconds (default 3600) rather than forever, so a reclaimed old slug cannot cause a cached redirect loop longer than that.
The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs as a single connection, not under real multi-connection contention.
Does not rewrite links inside your content, generate sitemaps or check slugs for offensive words; production database correctness and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: derived slugs suffix past taken/reserved (post-2); exact:true refuses non-canonical, reserved or taken input
old slugs redirect straight to the current slug and remain owned by their entity; renaming back reclaims one
options: routes, prefix, statusFor, redirectStatus: override route and statuses (default GET|HEAD {prefix}/:slug, 301)
maxLength (80 code points), separator (-), unicode (false), fallback (item), reserved

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/url-slugs.test.mjs tests/url-slugs-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: slugify lowercases, transliterates Latin diacritics, joins apostrophes, maps & to and and collapses punctuation to one separator
unicode mode keeps letters, digits and combining marks of other scripts while still transliterating Latin
slugify is idempotent for every BMP code point and a sample above in both modes, and every created slug resolves as current
slugs are cut at a word boundary within maxLength, and a single overlong word is hard-cut
input with no usable characters yields the configured fallback
a taken slug gets the first free numeric suffix, trimmed so the suffixed slug still fits maxLength
ten concurrent creates of one title get ten distinct slugs (memory store and PGlite unique key with retry)
reserved words and route names are refused as exact slugs and skipped when derived; the list is configurable
exact slugs must already be canonical; non-canonical input is refused with invalid-slug, never rewritten
rename keeps history; old slugs resolve to a redirect straight to the current slug, renaming back reclaims an old slug and no sequence produces a loop
old slugs cannot be taken by another entity; concurrent renames leave exactly one current slug
slugs are scoped per tenant and collection
SQL store quotes validated table names, so keyword and schema-qualified names work

HTTP adapter: 200 current, 301 with Location (query kept, finite private cache), 404 unknown or other tenant, 403 without scope, 405, 400 malformed encoding; routes, prefix, statusFor, redirectStatus and locationFor overrides

changes: First release: core, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch resolve adapter.
